jobs.title: Principal Remediation Consultant
jobs.description:
Principal Consultant - Site Investigation & Remediation

Bay Area, California

Compensation: $160,000 - $220,000 base salary + bonus potential

About the Opportunity

Our client is a globally recognized engineering and environmental consulting firm seeking a Principal Consultant
to support and expand its environmental practice in the Bay Area. This is a leadership-focused role for a technically strong consultant who thrives in client-facing environments and enjoys balancing project delivery, business development, and team leadership.
The ideal candidate will bring a background in engineering, geology, or environmental science
, along with extensive experience leading complex site investigation and remediation
projects. Candidates with experience providing litigation support and expert technical opinions
are highly encouraged to apply.
This position offers the opportunity to influence strategic growth, develop high-performing teams, and work on challenging environmental projects across a diverse portfolio of private and public-sector clients.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and oversee complex site investigation, remediation, and environmental compliance projects.
Manage project teams, budgets, schedules, and technical deliverables while ensuring high-quality client service.
Develop and maintain strong client relationships, serving as a trusted advisor on environmental and regulatory matters.
Identify, pursue, and secure new business opportunities through networking, proposal development, and client engagement.
Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior and mid-level staff.
Support strategic growth initiatives within the Bay Area and broader regional market.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across environmental, engineering, and scientific disciplines.
Provide technical support for environmental litigation, insurance claims, cost recovery actions, and expert witness services when applicable.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science
, or a related field.
12+ years of environmental consulting experience
with a strong emphasis on site investigation and remediation.
Proven success managing environmental projects from proposal through completion.
Demonstrated business development experience, including client management, proposal preparation, and revenue generation.
Experience leading, mentoring, and developing technical staff and project teams.
Strong understanding of federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
California professional registration (PE, PG, CHG, or related credential) is preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience providing environmental litigation support, technical expert services, or expert witness support.
Established client relationships within the Bay Area environmental consulting market.
Experience managing large remediation programs for industrial, commercial, energy, manufacturing, or public-sector clients.

Why Join?

Opportunity to join a respected international engineering and environmental consulting firm

Strong emphasis on internal career development and leadership growth

Flexible and collaborative working environment
Diverse and technically challenging project portfolio
Competitive compensation and performance incentives
401(k) with employer match

Access to multidisciplinary expertise and global resources while maintaining a local-market presence

jobs.title: Water Resources EIT
jobs.description:
Communities everywhere share the need for clean water. And as they work to meet that need, they’re facing new, more complex challenges every day. Our water professionals collaborate to contribute innovative ideas, guided by scientific rigor and a vision for sustainable growth. Every day, we’re helping communities improve, reuse, and protect our world’s most precious resource.

Join our team to deliver transformational projects that will benefit future generations. Grow with us, H2O+U.

Your Opportunity

Stantec is seeking a Water Resources EIT to join our multidisciplinary team in Sacramento, California. You will apply and grow your understanding of water resources engineering, analysis, and planning to help answer our clients’ water resource management questions.

We’re looking for inquisitive professionals who are passionate about water and bring experience in one or more areas of water resources engineering and planning—such as engineering analysis and design, modeling of physical systems (hydrology, water operations, reservoir and river temperature, hydrodynamics), or integrating technical analysis and stakeholder input into water management planning and decision-making. Our Water Resources team in California tackles the State’s water problems from drought resilience to climate change vulnerability. This role will support water resources planning and management and infrastructure projects for local, regional, state, and federal water-related agencies and organizations throughout California and other locations. As the successful candidate, you will use your technical abilities to assist in a wide variety of projects in a dynamic planning and design team setting.

Are you ready to advance your career with a collaborative team that puts people first, lives its corporate values, and works on some of the most challenging water projects in the world?

Your Key Responsibilities

Participate in multi-disciplinary teams on water resources projects across California.
Conduct technical evaluations supporting planning and design of water supply, flood risk management, and ecosystem/fisheries restoration projects.
Assist with project management activities associated with the planning and execution of water resources planning and engineering projects.
Coordinate with project managers, project engineers, other resource specialists (biologists, economists, etc.), clients, regulatory agencies, and subcontractors.
Tasks may include performing feasibility studies, water (hydraulic, hydrologic, or system operation) modeling, engineering calculations, preparing planning and technical engineering reports, research, data entry.
Analysis of water resources management issues and infrastructure at local, regional, and statewide scales.
Assist with preparing reports, gathering information, drafting proposals, drafting correspondence, completing progress reports, and conducting project management.
Support engineering and senior project staff in producing high-quality work products for our water clients.
Maintain consistently high standards of delivery, quality, flexibility, and innovation.
Assist with site visits and field investigations as necessary.
Perform other duties as required.

Your Capabilities and Credentials

An understanding of water resources planning, management, and design, such as: - Water allocation, reservoir operation, water system hydrologic and temperature models
Engineering feasibility analysis and design
Hydrology and hydraulics
Integrated water management, including water systems and hydrologic modeling
Water resources planning and decision-support processes, including stakeholder engagement
Planning and design of water resources infrastructure, including conveyance, groundwater and surface storage, pumping, and treatment facilities.
An understanding of California water resources (including river systems/water-related infrastructure and applicable laws/policies/regulations) and federal/state planning processes
Proficiency with Microsoft Office software including Word, Excel, and Access.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including public speaking experience.
Commitment to client satisfaction and the delivery of high-quality work products.
The ability to multi-task, prioritize, and take direction.
Strong interpersonal abilities for working in diverse team environments with staff, clients, and stakeholders.
Geographically based in California or willingness to relocate.
Typical office environment working with computers and working at a desk for extended periods of time.
Field work may include exposure to the elements including inclement weather.
Candidate must be willing and have the ability to travel, and on occasion, spend time working away from home office.

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Civil, Environmental, Bioresources or Agricultural, or Water Resources Engineering, hydrology, or related field. Advanced degree desirable.
Must have taken and successfully passed the FE exam and be an EIT or ability to obtain registration within 6 months required, or other professional certification/registration in appropriate field of expertise.
0-5 years of experience in the planning, design, and/or permitting of water resources, stormwater management, municipal water, and/or wastewater infrastructure
Must have a safe driving record and valid Driver's License.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee and other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

Stantec is a place where the best and brightest come to build on each other’s talents, do exciting work, and make an impact on the world around us. Join us and redefine your personal best.

Pay Range

Locations in CO, HI, IL, MD & Various CA, NJ, VA Areas-$85,000.00 - $123,300.00 Annually

Pay Transparency:
In compliance with pay transparency laws, pay ranges are provided for positions in locations where required. Please note, the final agreed upon compensation is based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. At Stantec certain roles are bonus eligible. Actual compensation for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on the agreed number of working hours per week.

Benefits Summary:
Regular full-time and part-time employees (working at least 20 hours per week) have access to medical, dental, and vision plans, a wellness program, health saving accounts, flexible spending accounts, 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase program, life and accidental death & dismemberment (AD&D) insurance, short-term/long-term disability plans, emergency travel benefits, tuition reimbursement, professional membership fee coverage and paid family leave. Regular full-time and part-time employees will receive ten paid holidays in each calendar year. In addition, employees will be eligible to accrue vacation between 10 and 20 days per year and eligible for paid sick leave (and if more generous, in accordance with state and local law).

Temporary/casual employees have access to 401(k) plans, employee stock purchase program, and paid leave, in accordance with state and local law.

The benefits information listed above may not apply to union positions because benefits for such positions are governed by applicable collective bargaining agreements
